 2027 Proton S70 RS revealed – turbo facelift gets new interior, Sportline top variant with quad tailpipes, red trim
 In Cars , Local News , Proton / by Jonathan Lee / 5 November 2026 10:23 am 
 -->
 Well, it’s official. Just weeks after Geely launched the facelifted fourth-generation Emgrand in China, Proton has gone ahead and pulled the covers off its twin, the facelifted S70 . The refreshed segment-straddling sedan gains the RS suffix – confirming an earlier rumour – that deputy CEO Abdul Rashid Musa says stands for “Refined Sportiness”.
 The version you see here is a look-faster variant called the Sportline that receives all the same upgrades as its Middle Kingdom sibling, but with the aggressiveness turned up to 11. Leading the charge is a bespoke new grille that ditches the chrome surround and expands beyond even the headlights, which themselves are the same LED projector units with bulb indicators as on the current MC1 .
 The larger aperture with silver rectangular pins joins the Emgrand’s boxier X-shaped bumper. The full-width, bone-shaped insert gets a sportier design with fake honeycomb mesh intakes on either side (the same motif can be seen in the downturned centre intake) and red strips, while a gloss black splitter has sprouted underneath.
 At the rear, the redesigned rear bumper gains (also fake) corner vents and a redesigned valance with the same honeycomb pattern and X50-style quad tailpipes; the boot lid spoiler with a central underbite appears to have been carried over from the MC1 Flagship X’s bodykit.
 The look is finished off with black side skirts with more red strips, a gloss black finish for the roof, door mirrors, door handles and window trim, and new 17-inch grey alloy wheels that hide red brake callipers, shod with the same GitiComfort F22 tyres as the MC1. Strangely, despite the RS branding, the only RS badge is on the boot lid; the grille and side skirts of the Sportline feature the same S badge as the X50 Flagship’s “Batmobile” rear wing.
 Inside, the RS gains a completely redesigned dashboard similar to the also-facelifted X50. That likely means that the S70 receives the same new screens – a slimmer 8.88-inch instrument display and a much larger 14.6-inch infotainment touchscreen. Here, the ambient lighting gets the same honeycomb pattern found elsewhere around the car.
 The centre console has actually been carried over from the new fifth-generation Emgrand, specifically the Emgrand L EM-i plug-in hybrid. That means you get new rectangular air vents, twin smartphone trays with a driver’s side Qi wireless charger and a Proton eMas 7 -style control knob flanked by physical air-con temperature and fan speed toggles.
 To make space for these items, the S70 comes with a steering column-mounted gear selector, also from the X50. This does unfortunately mean you lose the sequential shifter of the old S70 (even the new naturally-aspirated model with a CVT has it), and there are still no paddle shifters. The red highlights, including the lower dash, centre console, seat upholstery and even the seat belts are likely exclusive to the Sportline.
 While the said variant looks sportier than ever before, it brings no actual added performance to the table, soldiering on with the 181 PS/290 Nm 1.5 litre i-GT turbo four-cylinder engine added to the MC1 just this year. Paired with the same seven-speed wet dual-clutch transmission, it gets from zero to 100 km/h in an identical 7.5 seconds.
 The Sportline will likely replace the Flagship in the S70’s lineup, and given that the official photographs show the car without a sunroof, we assume that the Flagship X has been dropped. We expect the Premium to be retained with the same redesign but without the bodykit and red highlights. Hopefully, the lower-priced variant will gain advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), which is not the case with the outgoing model.
 Proton has yet to confirm pricing or when the RS will be launched, only that it will be presented at a fashion showcase by a “renowned local fashion designer” on November 10. The car will be sold concurrently with the NA variants that carry over the MC1’s unchanged styling. For now, what do you think about the new, rather extroverted look? Let us know in the comments.

 I don’t know, man… Maybe it’s because the photos were taken in a studio with heavy editing, but the overall design somehow manages to look like an upgrade and a downgrade at the same time.
 I have to give PROTON credit for the wheel design, though. However, the proportions don’t quite look right for a 17-inch setup. I think this design would look much better with an 18-inch setup. That said, we’ll have to wait for actual photos to see how it looks in person.
 As for the new interior, I feel it doesn’t complement the exterior design, especially with the red accents. Why not just go with an all-black interior with red stitching, similar to the X50 Sport Edition, but without the additional logos? Or is PROTON deliberately holding back that combination for a potential S70 Sport Edition in the future? Also, the LIM button still appears to be missing from the steering wheel, which makes the overall layout look somewhat incomplete.
 Another thing that bothers me is the inconsistent RS and S badging. Why does the rear get an RS badge while the front grille and side skirts only get an S badge? I know X50 has an S badge on its wing, but that’s different because it isn’t marketed as an X50 RS. Hopefully, PROTON has a proper explanation for this. Unless they’re introducing a new Racing Division under the S branding, this inconsistent badging just comes across as a rather cheap attempt at sporty branding.
 More importantly, I hope PROTON confirms that the S70 RS comes with paddle shifters during the official launch, because I haven’t spotted any in the photos released so far. The upgraded suspension also needs to be more than just a marketing point. It doesn’t necessarily have to be a multi-link setup, but at the very least, I hope Geely has given PROTON the freedom to fine-tune the suspension and handling characteristics to suit the car.
 They also need to address the existing throttle response, particularly the jerky, delayed and sluggish acceleration when moving off from a complete standstill. A better braking setup would be another welcome improvement.
 Otherwise, this risks becoming nothing more than a cosmetic package with questionable execution. PROTON could have done much better by developing its own front bumper design instead of simply adding honeycomb mesh to the existing facelifted Emgrand front bumper. A wider, continuous lower air intake, properly integrated and symmetrical side air vents and a complete chrome delete across the front grille and bumper would have given the front end a much cleaner, more aggressive and cohesive appearance.
 At this point, I really hope there’s more to the S70 RS than what these photos are showing. If the upgrades are mostly cosmetic, along with an interior update that comes with a questionable choice of colour scheme, then I think PROTON has missed a good opportunity to make this a genuinely worthwhile RS variant.
